title: Design parallel job execution, review it, then build it
summary: Write a design doc in docs/design for running independent jobs concurrently (bounded workers, reusing job and repo locks), including landing each job as its own branch/PR. Get an independent review recorded under docs/design/reviews, then implement in `athena go` with tests and docs.

defaults_applied.how: Design doc with alternatives (threads vs processes, serialized vs concurrent landing) and an independent review precede the build.
New tests run fake-agent jobs concurrently and cover landing; cargo test and clippy are clean.
All code and tests in Rust.
Docs, README, CHANGELOG and decision entry written for outside readers.
Behavior is checked by running cargo test and `go --help`.
Concurrency limit and kill switch enforced in code, not prose.

assumptions: Parallelism is inside one `athena go` invocation (several jobs or --all), using threads with a bounded worker count, not separate processes.
Landing stays serialized under the repository lock, but each parallel job lands as its own branch/PR via the existing native-PR landing path.
The independent review is a written review file under docs/design/reviews, produced before implementation, and the design doc records its findings.
Single-job `athena go <job>` output and exit codes (0 landed, 2 not landed, 1 error) stay unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new design doc under docs/design covers concurrency model, worker bound, lock use, kill switch and budgets, failure isolation, alternatives considered, and landing each parallel job as its own branch/PR.
A review file under docs/design/reviews records an independent review of the design, and the design doc shows how its findings were handled.
docs/decisions.md has an entry for the choice and alternatives; README, CHANGELOG and docs/design/athena-v0.md (command table) describe the new behavior.

Run `cargo test`: it passes, including a test where at least two fake-agent jobs run through the parallel path with a barrier or overlapping intervals proving concurrency, and both reach a terminal state.
Run `cargo test`: a test shows parallel jobs touching different files each land on their own branch/PR with records intact, and conflicting jobs end stale or blocked, never merged silently.
Run `cargo test`: a job locked by another process is reported for that job without aborting the others, and the kill switch stops every parallel job.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: both are clean.
Run `cargo run -p athena-cli -- go --help`: it documents the multi-job option and the concurrency limit.
Single-job `athena go <job>` keeps its output and exit codes; multi-job output has one line per job and exits 2 if any did not land.

out_of_scope: Running multiple jobs across separate processes or machines.
Changes to governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, CI workflows, lint config).
departures: Request spans design, independent review and a core concurrency build, so cost and time are well above the reference, which reflects mostly small jobs.
